Chapter 7: Humility — The Doorway to Deeper Relationship
You know, humility is often misunderstood. People sometimes think it means putting yourself down, or acting like you’re less than you really are. But true humility? It’s actually about being honest with ourselves—knowing who we are, and just as importantly, who we’re not, in the light of God’s greatness.
It’s about letting go of pride. Admitting when you need help. Being willing to receive what you honestly can’t get on your own.
Picture this: maybe you’ve always been the strong one. The person others rely on. You’ve worked hard, pushed through, and built your life on determination and grit. Then, out of nowhere, life knocks you off your feet—a painful loss, a failure, something you simply can’t fix. Suddenly, all those old strategies just aren’t enough.
That moment? It can feel crushing. No one likes to admit weakness, or ask for help, or let others see where we’re struggling. But here’s the thing—that’s exactly where humility is born. It’s when you realize it’s okay to need, to depend, to accept support. The walls start to crumble, and you discover the doorway to deeper, more genuine connection.
Humility isn’t just about admitting weakness, though. It’s also recognizing our limits—knowing we don’t understand everything, that we can’t control every outcome, and that we desperately need grace. It’s about listening, learning, and staying open to change.
Most of us, let’s be honest, resist this. We like to think we’re in control. But if we hold onto that illusion, the cost is real—loneliness, frustration, and feeling distant from God.
The beauty of humility is that it creates space for God to step in. When our hearts are open and our pride is set aside, God gives us what we truly need. And this isn’t about beating ourselves up or feeling ashamed. It’s about being honest, vulnerable, and willing to trust.
Sometimes, humility is learned in community. Maybe you’re the one who's always been the leader. But then, suddenly, you need support. It’s humbling—yet it’s also freeing. The masks drop, and real, authentic connection starts to happen. For others, humility shows up in moments of failure, when plans fall apart and the only way forward is starting over.
Here’s something to remember: humility isn’t just a box you check once. It’s a daily choice—a posture of openness and dependence. It means letting go of the urge to be right, or to control everything, or to have all the answers.
Humility is the willingness to be led, to be taught, and to be changed—over and over again.
